description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: lib/MIME/Base64.pm encode_base64 (a `for (my $i = 0; $i < $len; $i += 3)` loop of ord/substr/shift/array lookups/`.=`, then `s/(.{1,76})/$1$eol/g`); decode_base64 (`_b64_significant`'s `tr{A-Za-z0-9+/=}{}cd` -- #4981's per-call O(n^2) complement -- then a 4-char loop).  PCL runs the shim at about perl's speed on the same text; the gap to perl is that perl uses XS.

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/shim/shimbench.pl; quiet numbers legs/leg4.log): encode_base64 of 1,000 bytes: PCL 150 us, perl-running-the-shim 130 us, perl XS 0.6 us; decode_base64 of a 16-char string: PCL 22 us, perl-running-the-shim 2.5 us, perl XS 0.05 us (the decode gap is #4981).
Prevalence: 56 encode_base64/decode_base64 sites in 23 files (HTTP-Message, URI, MIME handling, Data::Dumper-ish tools).

THE FIX: a `builtin::` primitive pair over byte strings (a char > 255 dies with perl's "Wide character in subroutine entry"), the shim keeping its argument handling ($eol, the 76-column split, encoded_/decoded_base64_length, the url variants).  Do #4981 first: it alone takes decode to ~2-3 us.

BAR: the everyday + board rows that use it, guard rows with perl's output for '', 1, 2, 3, 57, 1000 bytes, an $eol of '' and of "\r\n", padding garbage on decode, a wide char; the measurement reproduced.

=== QUIET NUMBERS (s540b legs/leg4.log, load 1.1-1.4) === encode_base64(1K): PCL 125,956 ns, perl running the shim text 129,053, perl XS 529; decode_base64 (16 chars): PCL 18,556, shim-under-perl 2,394, XS 45.
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): MIME::Base64's shim encodes 3 bytes per Perl loop iteration -- 150 us per KB under PCL (perl's XS 0.6 us; perl running the same shim text 130 us); a `builtin::` base64 primitive is a few dozen lines of Lisp (decode is mostly #4981's tr cost)
